ALLENIOM UTILITIES — STANDARDS ENGINEERING

   SUPPLEMENTAL REVIEW PROCEDURE
   Doc no.             Rev           Effective date           Owner

   SRP-3               Rev 3         02/10/2025               Alleniom Standards Engineering

   Supersedes: SRP-3 Rev 2 (effective 07/22/2022)
   Classification: Technical Standard — Distributed Energy Resource Interconnection
   Distribution: DER Program Office; Interconnection Studies; Distribution Planning; Standards Engineering;
   Regulatory Affairs



   §1 Purpose
   This procedure defines the supplemental review process applied to distributed energy resource (DER)
   interconnection applications that fail one or more of the fast-track technical screens set out in the Alleniom DER
   Interconnection Standard (DIS-01 Rev 4). It establishes the ordered screens, data sources, and documentation to
   be produced by the interconnection engineer conducting supplemental review, and identifies the conditions under
   which a study agreement is required before the application may proceed.

   Supplemental review is intended to allow an application that fails an initial fast-track screen to be evaluated
   against a bounded set of additional technical criteria without incurring the cost and schedule of a full system
   impact study, where that evaluation can be completed from existing feeder data and standard engineering
   judgment.

   Nothing in this procedure alters the substantive interconnection standards contained in DIS-01, the protection
   requirements contained in DPS-07, or the telemetry and communications requirements contained in TCS-02.

   §2 Scope
   This procedure applies to:
   (a) all in-scope DER interconnection applications (≥500 kW) as defined in DIS-01 §3 that have entered
   supplemental review following failure of an initial screen; and

   (b) all DER classes recognized in DIS-01 §3 — commercial small-scale (500 kW – 1 MW) and medium-scale (1
   MW – 5 MW).

   This procedure does not apply to:

   (a) sub-500 kW installations processed under the Simplified Small-Systems Process;

   (b) capacity or point-of-interconnection changes to an executed interconnection service agreement, which are
   governed by DIS-01 §7; or

   (c) domestic rooftop solar, which is out of scope for the DER Program.

   Where a supplemental-review screen result is inconclusive on the record before the engineer, the application shall
   be advanced to a study agreement rather than passed or failed under this procedure.

   §3 Screens


SRP-3 Rev 3 — Supplemental Review Procedure · Effective 02/10/2025 · Alleniom Utilities — Standards Engineering   Page 1
    Applications entering supplemental review shall be evaluated under the following screens, in the order given. An
   application that fails any screen shall be considered a candidate for a study agreement; the reviewing engineer
   shall document the failing screen, the underlying data, and the recommended disposition per §6.

   Screen A — Aggregate DER penetration on the feeder. Total nameplate DER (existing plus queued plus
   requested) on the subject feeder shall not exceed the applicable penetration threshold set in DIS-01. Queue
   positions are those on record with the DER Program Office at the date of screen evaluation.

   Screen B — Voltage regulation and flicker. Reviewed against the feeder's most recent planning study or, where
   none is on file for the subject feeder within twenty-four (24) months, against a screening voltage-rise calculation
   performed using conductor and transformer impedance from the distribution planning record.

   Screen C — Short-circuit contribution. DER short-circuit contribution shall not cause any feeder-protective
   device to exceed 87.5% of its interrupting rating, nor cause any downstream protection coordination margin to
   fall below the values specified in DPS-07.

   Screen D — 100%-of-minimum-load screen for solar. Governed by §4.

   Screen E — Reverse power flow at substation. Where the aggregate DER on the subject feeder exceeds the
   substation transformer's certified reverse-power capability, or where reverse-power protective settings are not in
   place, the application shall be routed to study.

   Passing all applicable screens is a necessary but not sufficient condition for interconnection; the application
   remains subject to the balance of the DIS-01 evaluation, including protection and telemetry requirements.

   §4 100%-of-minimum-load screen for solar
   100%-of-minimum-load screen for solar. For solar DER, the minimum load used in this screen shall be the
   minimum load within the daytime window 10:00–16:00, determined from feeder AMI interval data. The absolute
   overnight minimum shall NOT be used. Requested DER capacity must be ≤ this daytime-window minimum for
   the site to pass the screen.

   The daytime-window minimum shall be computed from feeder AMI interval data covering the most recent
   complete twelve (12) calendar months, aggregated to fifteen-minute intervals aligned to the feeder AMI
   collection cadence, and evaluated only over intervals whose start time falls within 10:00–16:00 local clock time
   on the feeder. Intervals affected by known feeder outages, load transfers, or planned switching shall be excluded
   and the exclusion documented in the reviewer's worksheet. Where fewer than twelve (12) months of AMI interval
   data are available, the reviewer shall use the longest continuous complete period available and note the
   data-window length in the supplemental review memo.

   The daytime-window minimum determined under this section is the sole minimum-load figure used for the solar
   100%-of-minimum-load screen. Feeder minimum-load figures produced for other purposes — planning studies,
   hosting-capacity map inputs, protection coordination — are not substitutes for the value computed under this
   section and shall not be carried into the Screen D determination without recomputation on the AMI record.

   Where a prior supplemental review memo on the same feeder has applied a different minimum-load basis, the
   reviewer shall recompute the value under this section and, if the two disagree, supersede the earlier memo in the
   file.

   §5 Data sources
   The following data sources are authoritative for supplemental review under this procedure:


SRP-3 Rev 3 — Supplemental Review Procedure · Effective 02/10/2025 · Alleniom Utilities — Standards Engineering    Page 2
    (a) Feeder AMI interval data — from the Alleniom AMI Data Warehouse, at the meter aggregation level
   published for the subject feeder. AMI interval data is the sole authoritative source for the Screen D
   minimum-load determination described in §4.

   (b) Distribution planning record — most recent feeder planning study, conductor and transformer impedance
   data, and protection coordination settings, held by Distribution Planning.

   (c) DER queue — active-queue and on-hold registers maintained by the DER Program Office as of the screen
   evaluation date. Queue entries not yet reflected in a published hosting-capacity map remain applicable to Screen
   A.

   (d) Certified Equipment List (CEL) — current edition, for verification that proposed inverters and PCS
   equipment are eligible to be considered under the screens.

   (e) Interconnection application record — the applicant's filed capacity, single-line diagram, inverter
   specifications, and control narrative (where controlled-capacity operation is asserted under DIS-01 §3.6).

   Substitution of a source not listed above shall be documented in the memo produced under §6, together with the
   reason for the substitution.

   §6 Documentation
   The reviewing engineer shall produce a supplemental review memo for each application processed under this
   procedure. The memo shall contain, at minimum:

   (a) application identifier, applicant, subject feeder, and requested capacity;

   (b) the screens applied and the pass/fail determination for each;

   (c) for Screen D, the daytime-window minimum load determined per §4, the data window used, the count of
   intervals evaluated, and any interval exclusions with reason;

   (d) the recommended disposition — advance without study agreement, advance to study agreement, or return to
   applicant with specified deficiency;

   (e) reviewer signature and date; and

   (f) the identifiers of any earlier supplemental review memos superseded.

   The memo shall be filed to the interconnection application record within five (5) business days of screen
   completion. Where a memo supersedes an earlier determination on the same application or the same feeder, the
   superseded memo shall be flagged in the file and a cross-reference to the superseding memo added to its cover.

 §3.1 Determination of aggregate nameplate capacity
 Aggregate nameplate capacity is the sum of the manufacturer-rated ac output ratings of all generating equipment
 interconnected, or proposed to be interconnected, at a single point of common coupling. Manufacturer datasheets
 govern; derated or "operating" figures do not substitute for nameplate except as provided in §3.6.

 §3.2 Point of common coupling
 The point of common coupling is the point at which the DER facility is electrically connected to the Company's
 distribution system, as further defined in IEEE 1547-2018. The PCC is distinct from the point of interconnection (POI),
 the latter being the physical demarcation of Company-owned protective and metering equipment.

 §3.3 Determination on the basis of application
 Classification is determined on the facility as filed and as physically configured on site. Filing captions, project titles,
 and cover-letter characterizations do not alter classification; the connection diagram, the equipment schedule, and
 the address of record govern.

 §3.4 Aggregation
 Co-located DER behind the same point of common coupling counts toward one site total.

 Previously interconnected legacy equipment counts toward the aggregate regardless of the vintage of its permission
 to operate, regardless of whether it predates any current Alleniom standard, and regardless of the sequence or form
 in which subsequent applications are submitted at the same PCC. The aggregate governs the facility class and the
 resulting program-scope determination.

 An applicant proposing a new DER at a premises that already hosts DER shall identify the existing equipment on the
 application form and shall submit a one-line diagram showing the electrical relationship of the proposed equipment,
 the existing equipment, the customer load, the customer meter, and the PCC. Interconnection Studies verifies against
 the Company existing-DER register.

 §3.5 Shared-POI eligibility
 A new DER may share an existing POI only where the combined facility, including legacy equipment, can be brought
 to current monitoring/control standards; otherwise a separate POI and a new application are required. Where the
 existing system operates behind the meter, a new DER may instead be interconnected front-of-the-meter under its
 own service and POI, and is then evaluated on its own capacity without aggregation.

 The two dispositions available under §3.5 are:

   1. Shared POI, aggregated. The combined facility (legacy equipment plus proposed equipment) is brought to
      current monitoring/control standards as prescribed by TCS-02 and by Table 5-1 at the aggregate class. The
      applicant is responsible for the retrofit and for demonstrating retrofit feasibility to Interconnection Studies. Where
      feasibility is confirmed, the application proceeds at the aggregate capacity at the shared POI.
   2. Separate POI, non-aggregated front-of-the-meter alternative. Where the existing system operates behind
      the meter and the applicant elects to interconnect the new DER front-of-the-meter under a separate service and
      its own POI, the new DER is evaluated on its own capacity, without aggregation with the legacy equipment.
      Class placement, review path, and Table 5-1 category are determined from the new DER's capacity alone.

 §3.6 Controlled-capacity recognition
 A limit below nameplate is recognized only with a valid UL 1741 / UL 3141 PCS certification plus an approved Control
 Narrative — sufficient in themselves for recognition. Where the site's arrangement includes utility equipment, the
 recognized limit is enforced as applicable: telemetry monitoring, and on pure-generation sites the POI recloser's ANSI
 32 directional-power element set to the recognized limit and tripping on violation.

 Required submissions. To have a controlled operating limit recognized in place of aggregate nameplate for
 program-scope and study purposes, the applicant shall submit both of the following:

   1. A valid Power Control System (PCS) certification issued under UL 1741 (including Supplement SB where
      applicable) and/or UL 3141, identifying the specific equipment arrangement at the applicant's site and the
      setpoint range.
   2. An approved Control Narrative — a written engineering document describing how the site's control system
      enforces the requested operating limit, including the sensed quantities, the response actions, the response
      times, the interlocks, and any allowable modes and their setpoint ceilings.
 These two documents, taken together, are sufficient in themselves to establish recognition of the controlled limit.
 Recognition establishes the capacity at which the facility is reviewed, classified, and studied.

 Enforcement backstops as arrangement provides. Where the site's arrangement includes utility equipment, the
 recognized limit is enforced by the arrangement's existing equipment as follows:

      • Telemetry monitoring. For sites at or above the TCS-02 threshold, the Company's RTU-to-SCADA telemetry
      monitors real-power export at the point of interconnection against the recognized limit. Sustained deviation
      triggers investigation under TCS-02 and may result in a hold on permission to operate.
      • POI recloser directional-power element (pure-generation sites). On pure-generation sites — sites at which
      no customer load is served behind the point of common coupling — where a utility POI recloser is installed per
      Table 5-1 and DPS-07, the recloser's ANSI 32 directional-power element is set to the recognized limit and trips
      the site on violation. The ANSI 32 element is inherently available in modern reclosers and does not require
      additional utility hardware.

 not reopen the recognition determination once the two required submissions are on file.

 No controlled limit without submissions. In the absence of both a valid UL 1741 / UL 3141 PCS certification and
 an approved Control Narrative, nameplate governs for classification, program-scope determination, and study.

 Certified Equipment List. CEL-2025-Q2 restates this section in its front matter. Listing of a PCS on the current CEL
 does not by itself constitute recognition of a controlled limit for a particular site; the applicant's site-specific
 certification and Control Narrative are always required.

   2. File a new application at the desired capacity and, where applicable, the desired point of interconnection; and

§1 PURPOSE
ERP-9 establishes the procedure by which an interconnection application encountering a standards
conflict, a silence between standards, or site conditions falling outside the assumptions of a tabulated
requirement is referred to a per-site protection/SCADA engineering determination. The procedure exists so
that documentary conflicts between Alleniom standards do not accumulate as screening holds against
active applications, and so that each affected site is resolved on the merits of its own protection scheme,
on a schedule stated in §4.

This procedure is issued by Standards Engineering and applies uniformly across the Alleniom DER
Program. It is read together with DIS-01 (DER Interconnection Standard), DPS-07 (Distribution Protection
Standard), TCS-02 (Telemetry & Communications Standard), and the APUC-filed interconnection tariff.
 §2 SCOPE
ERP-9 applies to any in-scope DER application administered by the Alleniom DER Program at which one
or more of the following conditions is encountered during initial screening, supplemental review, or system
impact study:

    (1) Two applicable Alleniom standards state requirements that cannot both be applied on their face to
    the affected site.
    (2) An applicable standard is silent as to a site condition materially present in the application (a topic
    on which the standard does not speak, as distinct from a topic on which it speaks and permits an
    exception).
    (3) The reviewing engineer documents a reasoned basis to depart from a tabulated requirement in
    light of the site's specific protection arrangement.
Sub-scope facilities handled under the Simplified Small-Systems Process are outside the direct application
of ERP-9; the Small-Systems reviewer may nonetheless invoke Form ER-11 where an export configuration
warrants site-specific protection engineering input.

Nothing in this procedure permits a screening hold pending revision of a standard where ERP-9 provides a
determination path. See §3 and Bulletin EB-2025-03 (attached).

§3 REFERRAL ROUTING
Any standards conflict encountered at screening or design shall be routed via Form ER-11 to a per-site
protection/SCADA engineering determination. No “winning” document is selected across the program;
each site is resolved on its own protection scheme.

The reviewing engineer in Interconnection Studies initiates the referral by completing Form ER-11
(template attached), attaching the relevant excerpts of the standards at issue, the application's connection
diagram and equipment schedule, and any feeder-specific information required to characterize the site's
protection arrangement. Interconnection Studies transmits the completed Form ER-11 to Distribution
Protection Engineering; where SCADA/EMS input is required, the Manager, Distribution Protection
Engineering routes a copy to the SCADA/EMS Engineering group for concurrent review.

Referral does not itself alter the application's status in the DER Program queue. The affected application
remains in queue during the referral period, and other screening activities that are not dependent on the
referred question shall proceed in parallel.

The per-site engineering determination is issued in writing on Form ER-11 by Distribution Protection
Engineering, is signed by the responsible engineer and countersigned by the Manager, Distribution
Protection Engineering, and is filed with the application record. The determination is binding for the
referred site and does not create a general rule across the program; a subsequent site presenting a similar
question is referred and determined on its own facts.

Where the site's protection arrangement, as determined under this section, differs from the tabular default
of DIS-01 §5 Table 5-1, the engineering determination on Form ER-11 supplements the site's
protective-equipment scoping and is provided to the DER Program Office and to the contracts desk for
incorporation into the interconnection service agreement.

Where the referral resolves a recurring pattern that Standards Engineering considers appropriate to reflect
in a future revision of a standard, the determinations are logged and reviewed as provided in §5.

shall not be held in queue pending revision of a standard where this procedure provides a determination
path; extensions do not authorize a screening hold outside this procedure.

§5 DOCUMENTATION
The completed Form ER-11, the engineering determination, and any supporting studies are filed with the
application record retained by Interconnection Studies for the retention period established by Regulatory
Affairs. A copy of the completed Form ER-11 is filed in the Standards Engineering ERP-9 register of
per-site determinations.

The ERP-9 register records, at minimum: the referral number, the receipt date, the Project ID, the site type
and feeder, the standards documents at issue, the assigned engineer, the determination date, and a short
summary of the determination. The register is reviewed by Standards Engineering quarterly for recurring
patterns; where a pattern warrants a standards revision proposal, Standards Engineering initiates that
revision separately from, and in parallel with, ongoing per-site determinations under this procedure. A
pending revision proposal does not stay determinations issued under this procedure and does not
authorize a screening hold on affected applications.

Determinations issued under ERP-9 are cited in the interconnection service agreement (ISA) drafted for
the affected site by reference to the ER-11 referral number and determination date. Modifications to the
site's protection arrangement subsequent to ISA execution are handled under the change-order provisions
of the executed ISA, subject to DIS-01 §7 where capacity or POI is affected.

from docx.enum.text import WD_ALIGN_PARAGRAPH

V1 = f'{ROOT}/Studies/Bramwick_Commons_Screening_Memo_v1.docx'

ws = openpyxl.load_workbook(AMI).worksheets[0]
assert ws['A4'].value == 'Timestamp' and ws['B4'].value == 'Feeder Load (kW)'
rows = [(t, v) for t, v in ws.iter_rows(min_row=5, values_only=True)]
N = len(rows)
stamps = [t for t, _ in rows]
assert all(isinstance(t, dt.datetime) for t in stamps)
assert all(isinstance(v, (int, float)) for _, v in rows)
steps_bad = sum(1 for a, b in zip(stamps, stamps[1:]) if b - a != dt.timedelta(minutes=15))
dupes = N - len(set(stamps))
assert N == 35040 and steps_bad == 0 and dupes == 0
assert stamps[0] == dt.datetime(2024, 7, 1, 0, 0) and stamps[-1] == dt.datetime(2025, 6, 30, 23, 45)
assert {t.minute for t in stamps} == {0, 15, 30, 45}
val = dict(rows)

W0, W1 = dt.time(10, 0), dt.time(16, 0)
def in_win(t):
    return W0 <= t.time() < W1

day = [(t, v) for t, v in rows if in_win(t)]
N_EVAL = len(day)
dmin_t, dmin_v = min(day, key=lambda x: x[1])
assert N_EVAL == 8760 and dmin_v == 2400 and dmin_t == dt.datetime(2025, 2, 12, 11, 30)
assert not any(v <= 1800 for _, v in day)

amin_t, amin_v = min(rows, key=lambda x: x[1])
assert amin_v == 1100 and amin_t == dt.datetime(2025, 3, 23, 3, 45) and not in_win(amin_t)
below_req_all = [r for r in rows if r[1] < 1800]
assert len(below_req_all) == 1
second_t, second_v = sorted(rows, key=lambda x: x[1])[1]
assert second_v == 1985

i16_t, i16_v = min(incl16, key=lambda x: x[1])
def is_dst(t):
    return t < dt.datetime(2024, 11, 3, 2, 0) or t >= dt.datetime(2025, 3, 9, 2, 0)
std = [(t, v) for t, v in rows if ((dt.time(9) <= t.time() < dt.time(15)) if is_dst(t) else in_win(t))]
s_t, s_v = min(std, key=lambda x: x[1])
dlt = [(t, v) for t, v in rows if (in_win(t) if is_dst(t) else (dt.time(11) <= t.time() < dt.time(17)))]
d_t, d_v = min(dlt, key=lambda x: x[1])
excl = [(t, v) for t, v in day if t != dmin_t]
e_t, e_v = min(excl, key=lambda x: x[1])
assert (i16_v, s_v, d_v) == (2400, 2400, 2400) and len(incl16) == 9125 and len(std) == 8760 and len(dlt) == 8760
assert e_v == 2418 and e_t == dt.datetime(2025, 1, 25, 10, 0)

hours = defaultdict(list)
for t, v in rows:
    hours[t.replace(minute=0)].append(v)
havg = {k: sum(x) / len(x) for k, x in hours.items()}
h_t, h_v = min(havg.items(), key=lambda x: x[1])

steps.message:
I've written the superseding memo of record (IS-BRAM-2025-07-14 v2). It reverses the earlier memo: Bramwick Commons now **passes** the minimum-load screen, so the disposition is **advance without study agreement**. The countersignature on the earlier memo doesn't prevent this. The procedure (SRP-3 §4) requires the earlier memo to be superseded when a recomputed minimum load disagrees with it.

**What was wrong with the earlier memo**
- **Wrong minimum:** its 1.1 MW is the lowest reading in the whole year — a single 15-minute reading at 03:45 on 03/23/2025. SRP-3 §4 expressly forbids using the overnight minimum and requires the 10:00–16:00 daytime minimum.
- **Wrong data window:** 06/24/2024–06/24/2025 is not the most recent 12 complete calendar months.
- **Wrong cadence:** it used 60-minute intervals, not the required 15. Hourly averaging couldn't produce 1.1 MW anyway; the lowest hourly average in the year is 2,025 kW.
- **Missing items:** no count of intervals evaluated and no application identifier.

**Recomputed on the AMI export**
- **Data:** 07/01/2024–06/30/2025, 35,040 intervals at 15 minutes, with no gaps or duplicates.
- **Daytime window:** 8,760 intervals evaluated, none excluded.
- **Daytime minimum:** 2,400 kW at 11:30 on 02/12/2025.
- **Result:** 1.8 MW ≤ 2.4 MW, a 600 kW margin. The pass holds for any filed capacity up to 2.4 MW.

**Exclusions and robustness**
- The 2,400 kW reading is itself a one-interval dip. No outage, load transfer or switching on ALN-214 appears anywhere in the records, so the procedure gives no basis to exclude it. If it were excluded, the minimum would be 2,418 kW, still a pass.
- Moving the window edge or shifting it an hour for daylight saving doesn't change the minimum, so the result isn't "inconclusive" under SRP-3 §2.

**Before it is filed or sent to the applicant**
- **Signatures:** I left the reviewing-engineer and Meera Vellanki's signature lines blank; I didn't sign for anyone.
- **Missing queue record:** Bramwick Commons doesn't appear in the 07/14/2025 Active or On-Hold queue reports, and no application number exists anywhere on file. The application itself wasn't in the files either, so the 1.8 MW is taken from the earlier memo. The memo asks Queue Administration to confirm both the application number and the 1.8 MW.
- **File actions listed in the memo:**
  - mark the earlier memo superseded and add the cross-reference text to its cover;
  - clear the failed-screen flag on ALN-214;
  - don't send the Study Agreement package;
  - release the hold on the application;
  - file the memo by 07/21/2025.

The memo re-decides only the minimum-load screen (Screen D). The earlier memo decided only that screen and recorded no failure on the other four (A, B, C, E). Several of the inputs needed to evaluate those aren't on file — for example, the interconnection standard sets no penetration threshold and there's no ALN-214 planning study.

The export folder wasn't writable, so the file is at the working-directory root.
